EN: With the correct equipment, a vessel can transmit its science data back to Kerbin via CommNet. The \nhigher the signal strength, the more science results from the transmission. It’s always better to return \nthe data than to transmit it, but a strong Signal can make a lot of the difference.

CommNet uses soft occlusion where signals are not cut off immediately when the destination goes \nover the horizon. In addition, atmospheric bodies allow bouncing the signal through the atmosphere, \nfurthering the distance below the horizon a destination can be.
The signal strength is the product of the signal strengths of all links on the path back to the DSN \nor to a Control Point. For example:

With action groups you can cause multiple actions to happen at a single keypress. A common setup \nmight be to have all solar panels toggle on one keypress, or all radiators extend. With the layout seen \nhere you click on listed actions to alter the groups.
Part Actions: This shows the available actions for the part selected in the editor. If the part selected was placed using symmetry then the action will include all the parts in the symmetry group.
The Abort Action Group:\nThis stock group can be used to fire off your escape tower and save your crew in the event of a launch issue. Not \nsaying it's likely, but accidents do happen.
Group Actions: Actions listed here will be triggered when the highlighted group is activated.
Custom Groups: These let you define actions to occur when keys 1 to 0 are pressed.
Stock Groups: You can add to the stock actions through these items in the list.
Selecting a part in the scene causes it to be highlighted blue for identification

Moving Kerbals Around:\nYou can assign kerbals to positions by dragging them, or using the tick/cross buttons that are displayed when your \ncursor is over one. There are lots of ways to make sure you fill a seat, but you'll still forget sometimes.
